notes.title: Hotfix for Steam Overlay Crash
notes.content: [p]Hi Talisman fans! ːBlueTalismanː ːTalProToadː[/p][p]It's been a hot minute since we rolled out an announcement for [i]Talisman: Digital Classic Edition[/i], but today we launched a fresh patch for the game focused on resolving one issue - [b]the crash caused by playing the game with the Steam Overlay enabled.[/b][/p][p]You should be able to download it via Steam now - if anyone is still having issues with crashes after downloading the patch, please leave a comment on this announcement or send an email with your PC specs to support@nomadgames.co.uk[/p][p][/p][h3]An Update on the Talisman Steam Page[/h3][p]While we're talking about this patch, we wanted to touch on something that we'll be expanding upon fully in the future. Some of you will have noticed that back in February, the [i]Talisman: Digital Classic Edition [/i]base game was removed from the search directory in Steam. Since earlier this month, the game is now relisted in Steam search, as part of the [i]Talisman: Digital Classic Complete Collection[/i].[/p][p]These changes were made based on the feedback and popular demand that we heard from you all after the initial change. As for [b]why [/b]these changes happened in the first place, Talisman is a licensed product, so there are certain things that are out of our control when it comes to what's allowed to be listed on different storefronts, requirements for how we present our titles and how that impacts our ongoing licenses with the physical board game publishers we work with.[/p][p]Thanks to your feedback and some work on our end, we're pleased to be bringing back the previously removed from Steam search [i]Talisman: Digital Classic Edition[/i] store page, even if it's in a slightly different way than before. Going forward, we're going to be pushing for and doing what we can to come up with solutions that give you all the best outcome while fulfilling our requirements to our license owners.[/p][p]Thank you as always for your understanding and support! ːheartː[/p]

notes.title: Reaper Remastered Developer Blog - Talisman: Digital 5th Edition
notes.content:
Hi Talisman fans! ːBlueTalismanː

In case you missed it, we [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/247000/view/4596573778467909060?l=english]recently proudly announced[/url] that we’re going to be bringing expansions from [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] over to [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] once it launches, starting with [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i]. Not only that, but if you already own [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i], you’ll be able to access the remastered version entirely for free!

If you want to know when you’ll be able to play [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], the best way to do that is by adding it to your Steam wishlist!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/908060/Talisman_Digital_5th_Edition/

We shared some details about the process of bringing [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i] to [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] in that original announcement, but we figured you’d want to know more - so we’ve put together another developer blog, this time focusing on that process!

[h3][b]Deciding What to Adapt First[/b][/h3]
When it came to deciding which expansion from 4th Edition we wanted to bring over to 5th Edition first, we wanted to make sure we made the best choice possible for us as developers, and for you, our players. With 16 expansions to choose from, we had a lot of different elements to consider!

Thanks to 10 years of people playing [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i], we’ve got a ton of information about how players tend to play Talisman, the expansions they most often turn on/off during a game and much more beyond that. We also knew that certain expansions would take longer to implement in 5th Edition than others, so the complexity of the mechanics in the expansion was something we considered too - for example, implementing [i]The Clockwork Kingdom[/i] and its crafting system into[i] Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] would be a much bigger undertaking than adding [i]The Sacred Pool[/i].

After looking at all our options, we settled on starting with [i]The Reaper[/i] for a multitude of reasons. First of all, it’s a relatively simple expansion, from a mechanics point of view. It doesn’t add anything overly unique to the game aside from The Reaper himself, instead building upon the kind of mechanics already present in the base game. Instead of adding new mechanics, it instead adds balance to the adventure deck enhancing the base Talisman experience.

Secondly, we found that it is one of the most commonly enabled expansions among [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] players, even when players only enable a handful of expansions. Not only that, but across the different demographics we sort our players into (solo, online players, regular playgroups etc.), [i]The Reaper[/i] saw consistently high usage across all of them.

Also, [i]The Reaper[/i] was the first ever expansion we released for [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] all the way back in 2014, so it felt a bit poetic coming back to it as our first remastered expansion for [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i]!

[h3][b]Reaper Card Art Update[/b][/h3]
Anyone who’s taken a glance at the 5th Edition of Talisman will be able to tell you that the first thing that strikes you is the gorgeous artwork featured on all the cards. From the characters and items, to the enemies and strangers you encounter while playing, the entire game has a completely new look compared to the 4th Edition.

So, once we knew we were remastering 4th Edition expansions into Talisman: Digital 5th Edition, we knew we’d also want to update all the artwork to make it ‘fit’ with the new style of 5th Edition. However, we wanted to make sure that anyone who played the original 4th Edition version of the expansion would be able to tell at a glance what the card was.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031397/21306126c422fcde2a88bd8d4106f9a2badbe99c.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031397/d7f27f8a2487e00416b33ce5b30457302ad5b32a.jpg[/img]

So, in order to do this, we took each original piece of artwork in the original Reaper Expansion as a starting point, our art team would get to work on painting over it in a style that matches the artwork that you’d find in 5th Edition. This way, we made sure the creation of this new, painted card art would always be true to the original 4th Edition artwork, while still feeling like it was made for 5th Edition from the beginning!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031397/dcf2194f19bed0f4f5cfc2b738628a30c6cb1d88.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031397/6aa5ed82233d680f8f6766f85f1ba1f998f287a9.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Reaper Warlock Quests[/b][/h3]
One of the additions to Talisman that [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i] brings is ‘Warlock Quest Cards’ - instead of rolling a die to take one of 6 quests, you get to choose from 12 available quests at the Warlock Cave. However, the original 4th Edition versions of these cards only featured rules and flavour text, without any artwork. 

Seeing as we were remastering the expansion, we figured it would be a great chance to update these cards with artwork! That way, it’s easier to get across to players the ‘action’ they’re performing by completing whatever quest they’re carrying out. Check out some of the new Warlock Quest Cards below:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031397/a6fbe7f299992773ec837f09fb46b0b416d762a4.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Deck Editor Considerations[/b][/h3]
Another Talisman: Digital 5th Edition announcement we made recently was that we’d be including a Deck Editor - [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/908060/announcements/detail/4687773573364202806]you can check out all the details here if you missed it[/url]! 

As this is the first expansion we’ve added to [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], it meant this was the first time we had to figure out how expansions would work with the Deck Editor. You see, when playing with The Reaper Expansion physically, the rules instructed you to “Shuffle the new character, Adventure, and Spell Cards into their respective decks.” With this new digital Deck Editor however, we needed to figure out the best way to enable players to customise their game without breaking anything!

So, we were presented with two options:[list]
[*] Allow you to individually add The Reaper Expansion cards into the base game decks when editing your decks.
[*] Allow you to create custom decks just for [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i], which you could then choose between when you enabled the expansion.
[/list]Now, while it might seem that both of these options are practically identical, there is actually a major difference when it comes to our plans for the future of [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i]. You see, there are a whole group of cards from different expansions that really don’t work if you don’t have the mechanics from that expansion enabled during the game. For example, the Queen Mab from [i]The Woodland Expansion[/i] instructs you gain one Destiny when you encounter her. If we made it so that you could put Queen Mab into your Adventure Deck without [i]The Woodland Expansion[/i], she wouldn’t be able to perform that action.

Another thing we needed to consider was the sheer amount of cards that are going to be added to [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] in the future. Part of the reason we talk a lot about legacy code issues in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] making development difficult is due to us adding thousands of cards to the game over the last 10+ years. Rather than showing you each and every card at once and asking you to choose what you’d want to play with, having it so that you only need to worry about cards from [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i] when setting up your Reaper custom deck makes it much easier to manage. 

[h3][b]Making a New Reaper Model[/b][/h3]
Another highlight of The Reaper Expansion is the Reaper himself! Moving around the board and causing severely bad times for anyone he lands on, many would argue that he’s the defining feature of the Expansion. It is named after him, after all!

One of the changes between [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] and [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] is that we now fully 3D model all of the characters that are placed on the board - and that goes for The Reaper too! The good news is that The Reaper already has a real-life model, as he’s a miniature in the original 4th Edition expansion, so we had a very strong starting point for making our [i]Digital 5th Edition[/i] version.

We’re still polishing him up so he’s not quite ready to see just yet, but keep an eye out as we get closer to release!

And that’s the end of our latest [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] developer blog! We hope you’ve enjoyed this look at how we’re updating classic expansions for 5th Edition, and can’t wait to show you more of the game as development progresses.

To keep up with everything [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], make sure you follow us on [url=https://linktr.ee/nomadgames]all the places we are online[/url]!

And don’t forget to wishlist [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] to get notified when it launches!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/908060/Talisman_Digital_5th_Edition/

And you’d like to find out more about [i]Talisman: 5th Edition[/i], you can do so by going [url=https://www.warhammer-community.com/2024/06/07/talisman-returns-with-a-glorious-new-5th-edition-and-the-same-classic-gameplay/]here[/url]!

notes.title: Talisman: Digital Edition - DLC Carryover to 5th Edition Announcement and FAQ
notes.content:
Hey Talisman fans! ːBlueTalismanː

Today we’re excited to announce two very important things:
[list]
[*] We’re going to be bringing content from [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] over to [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], starting with [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i].
[*] Not only are we bringing existing DLC content over, but on the platforms that support it, if you’ve already purchased that content in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i], you’ll be able to play it in [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] completely free of charge!
[/list]
We’ll be sharing more information about release dates for both [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] and [i]The Reaper Expansion for Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] in the near future, so make sure to wishlist the game now to get notified of the latest news!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/908060/Talisman_Digital_5th_Edition/

The love and support we’ve been shown over the last 10 years while developing [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] has always overwhelmed us here at Nomad Games, and when creating [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], we knew we wanted a way to show our loyal Talisman fanbase that we massively appreciate that love and support. We also fully appreciate the financial commitment you’ve already made towards [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i], and want to show our appreciation.

This updated and remastered version of [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i] will feature all-new artwork, special avatars and titles for your Nomad Account and more (which we’ll reveal later on once development has progressed). To give you a sneak preview of what you can expect though, we’ve grabbed some of the brand-new artwork to show you the new look that you can expect to see in[i] The Reaper Expansion[/i] in [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i]!

Can you recognise some of the iconic Reaper cards below?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5076051/8e18a5d3630e097a552ff56614c7798fa5b68525.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5076051/692de349c9d490ead42c2ea7afc0874ae2f1aafb.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5076051/bc151d2ab03acfe4ba8e28d4cb158ce2ea7e71d3.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5076051/b0ee7a973e3b6c0253a06fccfc9b97746f44b226.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/5076051/707b375d903c87bcddfc2d830c737bf5fc1ad0ce.jpg[/img]

So if you’ve not picked up [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i] yet in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] (or any other expansions!), now you’ve got even more reason to add it to your Steam library. Right now we’ve actually got our biggest publisher sale ever happening over on Steam, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/nomad/sale/nomadgamespublishersale]so go check it out![/url]

We’ve spent a long time figuring out the logistics of exactly how we’ll give you access to your [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] content within [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], so we’ve put together a comprehensive FAQ that should hopefully answer any questions you might have! You can find it below.

And if anything hasn’t been covered, you can reach out to us on [url=https://linktr.ee/nomadgames]all the different places we are online![/url] Or leave a comment here on Steam - Tom will be lurking there, as always. ːeyeːːeyeː

[h1]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition - DLC Carryover FAQ[/h1]

[b][h3]How will you know I own the expansions in Talisman: Digital Edition?[/h3][/b]

Through your Nomad Account! Your Nomad Account (which is entirely free to sign-up for and use) keeps track of the expansions and extra content you own, so by signing into the same account on both versions of Talisman, we’ll be able to detect what you already own.

[b][h3]Does this mean prices are going up?[/h3][/b]

It does not! We’re not going to be increasing the prices of the existing content in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] on any platforms, anywhere. In fact, alongside this announcement we're running a publisher sale here on Steam, with some of our deepest Steam discounts on Talisman expansions ever. Check it out!

[h3][b]Will this only apply if you buy the expansion before it gets added to Talisman: Digital 5th Edition?[/b][/h3]

Nope! If you buy [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i] in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] after it’s been added to [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], you’ll just need to sign into the same Nomad Account on both [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] and [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i]. We’re not restricting access to expansions based on when they were purchased.

[h3][b]Will this work across all my devices?[/b][/h3]

Right now we’re still focusing on the Steam version of [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] only, so we can’t say for certain which platforms will allow you to bring across your existing expansions and other content.

We’re still a long way away from even being able to confirm any console versions of [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], so we won’t be able to talk much more about this topic until much further down the line. If/when we confirm console ports for [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], we’ll be sure to address this then - but until then, we haven’t had a chance to properly investigate it.

[h3][b]Will I still be able to get this Talisman: Digital Edition content in Talisman: Digital 5th Edition if I don’t own Talisman: Digital Edition?[/b][/h3]

One of the reasons we made the base game for [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] free on Steam earlier this year was because we wanted to make sure that if someone wanted to play [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] content in [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], that the process of doing so was as easy as possible.

So if you do want [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i], you’ll only need to download and boot up [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] once to sign into your Nomad Account - in the same way that you can currently sign into your Nomad Account on mobile and PC to sync your purchases!

[h3][b]Will we still be able to share expansions for free in online multiplayer?[/b][/h3]

Absolutely!

For those who don’t know, when you’re playing online in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i], only one person in the lobby needs to own an expansion for everyone else to be able to use it. We’re happy to confirm that this feature will continue into [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] - so only one person in the lobby will need to own [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i] to be able to play with it online.

[h3][b]When will 4th Edition expansions be added to Talisman: Digital 5th Edition?[/b][/h3]

A very good question! Right now we’re still in the process of developing [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i] for [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], but once we get closer to release we’ll have a much better idea of how long the porting process generally takes.

Once we’ve published [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i], we’ll be taking a look at what content we want to bring forward next. Depending on how long it takes us to port over [i]The Reaper[/i] and the next expansion we want to bring across, will depend on when the next expansion will be added.

[h3][b]How often will you be adding 4th Edition expansions to Talisman: Digital 5th Edition?[/b][/h3]

Again, this depends on how long porting an expansion takes! So we can’t give a definitive answer on this right now, but once [i]The Reaper[/i] is available in [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], we’ll share more plans about our next steps for bringing across expansions.

[h3][b]Will you still be able to try a Talisman: Digital Edition expansion each week for free?[/b][/h3]

You will!

For those who don’t already know, we currently have a weekly rotation of free-to-try expansions in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i], allowing you to try out all of the various expansions we’ve got available in the game. Even when we bring these expansions to [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], we’re not changing that!

We’re still figuring out how we’ll handle these weekly rotating expansions in [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], so we’ll share more about that in the future.

[h3][b]What are you going to do with cards/rules that don’t work in the 5th Edition rules?[/b][/h3]

For this, we’re going to be classifying cards into three distinct categories:
[list]
[*] Cards that work within the 5th Edition rules with no changes needed.
[*] Cards that still technically function within the 5th Edition rules, but no longer function as they should.
[*] Cards that no longer function/don’t have a purpose at all within the 5th Edition rules.
[/list]
For cards that fall within the 1st category, we won’t need to do anything. Huzzah! For cards in the 2nd category, we’re going to be looking at each card on an individual basis and adjusting its effects to make sure it follows the rules of 5th Edition, without changing how it works from a gameplay perspective.

The third category of cards is the trickiest for us from a design perspective, but it’s not an impossible task! If a certain card doesn’t work at all due to changes in rules between 4th and 5th Edition, we’ll look at what the card is trying to do, and the action/item/character the card is representing. We’ll then make a new version of that card that matches what the 4th Edition card was trying to originally do.

[h3][b]What about the DLC characters?[/b][/h3]

We’re planning on bringing across the [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] DLC characters over to [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] too! Right now our priority is porting expansions however, as we know that they’ll bring a lot more to the gameplay experience.

So stay tuned for more information on how we’ll be bringing across DLC characters! Oh, and they will also be free for anyone who owns them in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] already, of course.

[h3][b]What about the Legendary Decks?[/b][/h3]

For anyone who doesn’t know, the Legendary Decks in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] were a series of special decks that you could purchase for certain expansions that offered a higher amount of challenge for experienced players.

Given that Legendary Decks were specifically designed for more hardcore players as an extra challenge based on requests from our community, adding them to [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i] isn’t high on our priority list at the moment. We’d rather focus on bringing across content that we know more players will appreciate and enjoy before we focus on something more niche like the Legendary Decks.

Not to say that it’ll never happen, but we’ve got a lot more stuff we want to get through first!

[b][h3]Does this mean content is being removed from Talisman: Digital Edition?[/h3][/b]

Nope. Not at all.

You’ll still be able to play [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i] in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] as you have previously. Once we bring [i]The Reaper Expansion[/i] into [i]Talisman: Digital 5th Edition[/i], you’ll just have the choice between which version of Talisman you want to play it in!

And that’s the end of the FAQ! Like we said before, if anything hasn’t been covered, you can reach out to us on [url=https://linktr.ee/nomadgames]all the different places we are online![/url]

And if you’d like to make sure you keep up with all things Talisman: Digital 5th Edition, wishlist the game now!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/908060/Talisman_Digital_5th_Edition/

And you’d like to find out more about Talisman: 5th Edition, you can do so by going [url=https://www.warhammer-community.com/2024/06/07/talisman-returns-with-a-glorious-new-5th-edition-and-the-same-classic-gameplay/]here[/url]!

notes.title: Talisman: Digital Edition - Free-to-Play Announcement
notes.content:
Hey Talisman fans! ːBlueTalismanː ːheartː

Today we’re excited to announce that we’re going to be making [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] free to download and keep on Steam as of May 23rd!

Over the 10+ years since we originally launched [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] here on Steam, the game has gone on to become a favourite for millions of players across the globe. We’re hoping that making the base game of [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] free-to-play will introduce the game to a whole new wave of future Talisman fans.

We’re rolling out this announcement to make sure we you all an advanced warning that this change is going to happen. If you’ve already bought the game on Steam within the last week, you can automatically refund it via Steam Support, for example!

We also figured that a lot of you would have questions about this change, so we’ve put together a comprehensive FAQ that should hopefully answer any questions you might have! If anything hasn’t been covered, I'll be in the comments here on Steam replying, and you can reach out to us on [url=https://linktr.ee/nomadgames]all the different places we are online![/url]

[h2]Talisman: Digital Edition - Free to Play FAQ[/h2]

[b]Why are you doing this?[/b]

[i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] has been out for more than 10 years at this point, and over the years we’ve occasionally offered the game for free - either through giveaways or temporary free-to-keep periods on mobile. We’ve also had a close look at how players tend to play [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i], and we think that lowering the barrier to entry for the base game will bring in a whole new wave of players, and leave us in a better position to support Talisman going forward.

[b]What changes can I expect to see once Talisman: Digital Edition is free-to-play?[/b]

Very little! We might make a bit more use out of the news section on the main menu to direct you towards cool stuff we’re working on here at Nomad Games, but other than that the [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] experience is going to stay the same as it was (toads and all)! ːTalProToadː

[b]What features/content will be available for free, and what will I need to buy?[/b]

You’ll be able to play with the [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] base game, and we’re not going to put anything behind a paywall that was previously already in the base game. So you’ll still be able to play online, single-player against AI and access your Nomad Account. You'll also still be able to play with your friends, so if you've got buddies who've never experienced the joys of Talisman - now they've got no excuse!

[b]Will there be any in-game advantages for players who previously purchased Talisman?[/b]

Absolutely not. As random as Talisman can be, it’s important that everyone is treated fairly and have exactly the same odds of success or failure. This applies to dice rolls, card draws and everything else in the game. No player will ever be given an advantage over another in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i], no matter if they’ve previously purchased the game or are a free-to-play player, or for any other reason.

[b]I am a player who paid for the game before it goes free. Do I get my money back/do I get anything for paying for it?[/b]

[i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] has been out for over 10 years now, has been given away for free multiple times and also been in multiple game bundles, leading to the price for the base game (especially if you want to grab a Steam key) being very, very low. We’re still going to look into giving out something special for people who previously bought the game as thanks for supporting us, but we’re still figuring out exactly what that might/would look like.

While we’re aware that it can be frustrating to have something you paid for be made available for free later, we’re hoping that between your purchase of [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] and May 23rd, you feel like the game provided you enough entertainment to justify your purchase.

[b]Will there be ads or other interruptions in the free-to-play version?[/b]

Nope! We’re not going to make you wait, sit through ads or anything else annoying when you play [i]Talisman: Digital Edition.[/i]

[b]Will there be any restrictions or limitations for free players compared to paid players?[/b]

There will not be! If you’ve just picked up [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] for free and your friend has had [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] sitting in their Steam library since 2014, you’ll both have access to exactly the same game. The only difference will be your own access to expansions, characters and legendary decks based on what extra content you’ve purchased.

[b]Does this mean you’re going to add microtransactions to the game?[/b]

We’re not planning on adding any microtransactions to [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i]. You’ll still be able to purchase the same expansions, characters and Legendary Decks as you’ve been doing since the game launched - we’re not adding anything extra or hiding anything new behind a paywall.

[b]Will there be any incentives for players to spend money in the game?[/b]

Aside from what we’ve already had in the game for ages? Nope! You can still pick up expansions, characters, runestones and Legendary Decks if you want, but we’re not adding any extra incentives or anything that gives you an advantage over other players for money.

[b]Will there be any changes to multiplayer or matchmaking?[/b]

We’re anticipating that the move to free-to-play will increase the number of average active players in online multiplayer, so we’re going to be keeping an eye on our online servers to ensure they can handle the increased load. Other than that, we’re not making any changes to how multiplayer and online games function in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i].

[b]Will the game still be available on the same platforms?[/b]

We’re not going to be removing [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] from any storefronts, so anywhere you could get Talisman previously, you’ll still be able to get it.

We are planning on stopping support for the Mac version of [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] at some point soon in the future, but this isn’t actually anything to do with Talisman going free-to-play. This is due to the extremely low player counts for the Mac version (less than 1.5%!) and changes that Apple have made when it comes to making games work on Mac.

We’re not going to be taking away access to the Mac version of [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] though - we’re just not going to be rolling out any future updates for it.

[b]Are you going to be releasing more expansions for Talisman: Digital Edition then?[/b]

We’re not planning on releasing any more expansions for [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] at this time. We know there is a big demand for new Talisman content though, don’t worry! We’re working behind the scenes to see what exciting things we can bring to you all. So stay tuned. ːeyeː

[b]Is the game still going to get patches?[/b]

Yes it will! Our plan is to continue releasing patches for [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] that fix bugs, improve stability and overall make the game a better experience for you all.

[b]Will this change how expansion sharing works?[/b]

It will not! For anyone who doesn’t know, in [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] only one player in an online lobby needs to own an expansion for it to be usable in that game by everyone. So if you own all the expansions and just want to play them online with your friends who own nothing Talisman, they can now just download the base game for free and play along with you!

[b]I have an unredeemed Steam key for Talisman: Digital Edition, what would happen when I redeem it?[/b]

Not much! Steam does keep track of your key redemptions, and redeeming a key will mean you’ll be marked as an owner of [i]Talisman: Digital Edition - Retail Key[/i]. This will mean you have access to [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i], but so does everyone else once the game goes free - so the end result is the same.

[b]Won’t this mean that there will be more griefers and cheaters?[/b]

We’re going to be keeping an extra close eye on how people play [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i] online once we make the transition to free-to-play. The good news is that we’ve already had 10+ years of people trying to be rude to each other via Talisman. We’ve managed to get a pretty good handle on how to stop people from being mean to each other, so they’ll have to find somewhere else to shout at random strangers on the internet. (We’ve heard X is pretty good for that…)

And that’s the end of the FAQ! Like we said before, if anything hasn’t been covered, you can reach out to us on [url=https://linktr.ee/nomadgames]all the different places we are online! [/url]

Check out the full list below:
[list]
[*] Fixed a crash that was caused by clicking on the Omen Tracker icon when there's was no current omen
[*] Fixed a crash that would happen at the end of round when Kallind was discarding Adventure cards from the board 
[*] Fixed a crash caused by there being no valid player when evaluating whether [i]any[/i] spell could be cast at the beginning of a turn
[*] Fixed a potential crash when the game tries to get the Strength/Craft value for a card that's not an Enemy
[*] Fix for a crash caused by the Shapeshifter using their ability against a ghost, then winning their battle at the Crown of Command (talk about specific! 👻)

[*] Previously, you'd sometimes be able to join greyed-out lobbies that you shouldn't have been able to join if you clicked fast enough. We've now made it so you can't join those lobbies, no matter how fast you think your clicking skills are.

[*] Fixed the 'End of Days' cards not being properly added to the board when loading a save
[*] Fixed the Ageless Talisman not buffing player stats correctly
[*] Fixed the Jin Blooded being able to incorrectly bind spells cast by Ascendant Divine
[*] Fix a crash caused by switching to view the inner region in the Challenge For The Crown ending
[*] Fix a crash caused by moving a Terrain card that has a Denizen on it

notes.title: Talisman: Digital Edition Patch Notes - 12/09/2022
notes.content:
Hi Talisman fans! ːBlueTalismanː

Today we've rolled out the latest patch for [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i]. A good number of these fixes came about because [b]you[/b] reported them either on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/nomadgames]Discord[/url] or on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/247000/discussions/0/]Steam forums here[/url]. So from everyone working on Talisman here at Nomad Games, thanks for your help and support!

Check out the official patch notes below, and don't forget to download the update if you want to play with your friends - you all need to be on the same version to play together (including cross-platform play!)

[h2]General Fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] We’ve made it so that you can’t use the ‘No More Lives’ house rule while The Dancing Skulls ending is active. This is because during this ending, You can only resurrect if you have at least 1 life point which you can gain from defeating enemies (or trading in trophies depending on rule choice) or other card encounters. If you have the No More Lives rule switched on, you've basically made it incredibly difficult to get resurrected, to the point you're limited to 2 cards from the realm region's deck. So it could also become impossible to do so. So in order to avoid people getting stuck in this situation, we’ve made this change.
[*] Certain Legendary versions of cards weren’t causing challenges to trigger as they should, so we’ve gone ahead and fixed those cards. The Legendary Deck versions of Self Portrait, Wraith and Giant will now add to challenges when encountered.
[*] The Devil's Minion was previously unable to use weapon inventions during psychic combat despite the fact they can use regular weapons that are meant for psychic combat. We’ve fixed this, so now all you Devil’s Minion players can use invented weapons to your evil hearts content.
[*] We discovered and fixed an issue with the Witch Doctor's Evil Eye ability. If you land on a character in the centre space for the first time and there is someone already there, it's ok to use his ability. However, the game was allowing you to keep using his ability on the following turns despite not moving to land on the other character. We’ve fixed this now, so he can only use his ability when he lands on someone.
[*] A minor fix, but sometimes the Werewolf card wouldn’t appear properly when you encountered it - it should now be visible.
[*] We fixed an issue where the use of the Horn of Dread could lead to locking the game if the owner dies and then the new owner who uses it straight away loses a life.
[*] We fixed a bug with the Enlightened destiny card, where it would not give the player a chance to trade in 1 light fate to gain a spell. Even if the player had room for a spell in their inventory and there are no anti-spell/magic effects in play, the game still wouldn’t let them use it. This has now been fixed, and the Destiny should function properly.
[*] When the Ifrit Invasion card from the Fireland expansion was drawn while the Cataclysm version of the board was in use, the card wouldn’t let you roll for its effect. We’ve fixed this issue, so now the card should function as expected even when using the Cataclysm board.
[*] We’ve added some more localisation fixed based on feedback from the community - thanks to everyone who pointed out text that needed updating!
[/list]

[h2]Crash Fixes:[/h2]

We’ve rolled out a ton of crash bug fixes in this patch, including fixes for:
[list]
[*] An occasional crash downloading Avatar and Challenge textures
[*] An occasional crash when selecting cards in a network game
[*] An occasional crash in CURL on Android
[*] A very infrequent crash when saving the game
[*] And more!
[/list]

[h2]Nomad Account Updates:[/h2]

We’ve now added a ‘delete account’ button to the game, so that you can delete your Nomad Account directly through [i]Talisman: Digital Edition[/i]. Be careful with this feature however, as you won’t be able to get your account back!

We’ve also updated the email that we send when you sign up for a Nomad Account to enable email account verification. Previously you could enter any old email address and have a valid email address without needing to confirm that email was actually you. So now we’ve added a ‘confirm email address’ button to your email, so we can just confirm you are who you claim to be.

As always, thanks for the support everyone! ːheartː
